glossary.parathyroid hormone: Hormone from the four parathyroid glands that raises blood calcium.
glossary.parathyroid glands: Four small glands behind the thyroid that make PTH.
glossary.bone resorption: Breakdown of bone by osteoclasts, releasing calcium into the blood.
glossary.renal stones: Hard mineral deposits in the kidney or urinary tract.
glossary.fragility fractures: Fractures from a fall from standing height or less, due to weak bones.
glossary.postmenopausal: After the menopause, when periods have stopped.
glossary.carcinoma: A cancer arising from epithelial cells.
glossary.vitamin D deficiency: Too little vitamin D, so less calcium is absorbed from the gut.
glossary.autonomous: Working on its own, no longer controlled by normal feedback.
glossary.dehydration: Loss of too much body water.
glossary.proximal weakness: Weakness of the muscles near the trunk, such as the hips and shoulders.
glossary.pituitary: Gland at the base of the brain that controls many other endocrine glands.
glossary.Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia: Inherited syndromes causing tumours in several hormone-making glands.
glossary.peptic ulcer disease: Sores in the stomach or duodenal lining caused by acid.
glossary.reflux: Stomach acid flowing back up into the oesophagus.
glossary.biochemical: Based on blood or urine chemistry tests.
glossary.phosphate: A mineral handled alongside calcium; PTH makes the kidneys excrete it.
glossary.Technetium-99m: A radioactive tracer used in nuclear medicine scans.
glossary.urinary calcium: The amount of calcium lost in the urine.
glossary.renal function: How well the kidneys are working, measured by creatinine and eGFR.
glossary.hydration: Giving fluids, often IV saline, to correct dehydration and help the kidneys clear calcium.
glossary.total parathyroidectomy: Surgical removal of all the parathyroid glands.
glossary.allosteric: Binding at a site other than the main one to change how a receptor responds.
glossary.paracrine: Signalling to nearby cells rather than through the bloodstream.
glossary.renal tubular: Relating to the kidney tubules, where filtered substances are reabsorbed or excreted.
glossary.vitamin D: Vitamin that, once activated by the kidney, increases calcium absorption from the gut.
glossary.active vitamin D: Calcitriol, the form made by the kidney that acts on the gut and bone.
glossary.phosphate retention: Build-up of phosphate when failing kidneys cannot excrete it.
glossary.hypocalcaemia: Low calcium level in the blood.
glossary.neuropsychiatric: Affecting the brain's function, mood and thinking.
glossary.ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves; used in the neck to look for an enlarged parathyroid.
